data.summary: The 10‑week plan front‑loads the student’s weak units (Linear Momentum and Torque) with live class support, then cycles through the remaining units while keeping a steady 5‑hour weekly load. The final week is reserved for mixed review and timed free‑response practice to consolidate knowledge before the exam.

tasks: Read textbook sections on conservation of linear momentum and elastic/inelastic collisions.
Do 8 free‑response problems on momentum conservation; check answers with the scoring guide.
Create a one‑page summary sheet of momentum equations and collision types.

weeks.focus: Live class on Linear Momentum basics
tasks: Attend live class #10000 and take detailed notes on linear momentum and impulse.
Complete the class worksheet (10 problems) on 4.1 and 4.2.
Review class notes and redo 5 of the worksheet problems without looking at solutions.
Read sections on connecting linear and rotational motion and rotational inertia.
Solve 6 problems linking linear velocity to angular velocity (5.2).
Calculate rotational inertia for 4 different objects (5.4) and compare results.
Watch the AP review video on scalars/vectors and displacement/velocity/acceleration.
Do 12 free‑response questions covering 1.1 and 1.2; grade with the AP rubric.
Sketch motion graphs for three different scenarios and label key features.
Attend live class #10001; focus on rotational kinematics and torque definitions.
Complete the class’s problem set (8 questions) on 5.1 and 5.3.
Create flashcards for torque formulas and practice applying them to 4 new problems.
Read textbook chapters on systems, center of mass, and drawing free‑body diagrams.
Draw FBDs for 5 different systems and label all forces.
Solve 9 free‑response problems involving Newton’s third law and force decomposition.
Watch tutorial on translational kinetic energy, work, and potential energy.
Complete a worksheet of 10 problems covering 3.1–3.3.
Summarize the work‑energy theorem in a one‑page cheat sheet.
Read sections on rotational kinetic energy and torque‑work relationships.
Calculate rotational kinetic energy for 5 rotating objects (6.1).
Solve 7 problems that require converting torque to work (6.2).
Review density and pressure concepts; do 6 problems on 8.1 and 8.2.
Read about simple harmonic motion definitions and period formulas.
Complete 8 free‑response questions on SHM basics (7.1, 7.2).
Take a 60‑minute timed free‑response practice exam covering all units.
Mark the exam using the AP scoring guidelines; note any recurring errors.
Review error log and redo 5 missed problems from each weak unit (4 and 5).

data.final_week_advice: After the timed practice, focus on the specific question types that cost you points, review your summary sheets, and get plenty of rest the night before the exam. Confidence comes from knowing you’ve systematically tackled every unit and reinforced your weak spots.
